why we don't write prayers

three lines we never cross. they're the reason a Catholic Keeper and a Sikh Keeper will both let us in the door.

1. we never write a prayer

every prayer in infinite hill is that religion's own, from its own texts, in its own words. we read them to you; we don't compose them, improve them, modernize them, or "make them relatable." a prayer somebody at a startup wrote is not a prayer. it's copy.

2. we never blend

one door at a time. a lesson in Hinduism is Hindu, start to finish. a lesson on my own path uses wisdom stories from many places — and every one of them is tagged with where it came from, and none of them is folded into a teaching that pretends to be above all of them. eight doors, one house — not one soup.

3. we never compare

we don't rank, we don't reconcile, we don't say who's right. you'll never see a chart on infinite hill with religions in the rows. we teach each door the way its own people teach it and let you walk where you want. the one thing we'll say out loud is the one thing they all say: treat people the way you want to be treated.

why it matters

the moment we write a prayer, blend a teaching, or pick a winner, we've become a religion — a new, small, bad one. we'd rather be the house.

start now. it's free.
